themes_detail.label: Public Drinking Spike
themes_detail.summary: Public drinking complaints surged to 6 this week versus a baseline of 1.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 380% spike (z-score: 3.96)—signaling a possible emergence of street-level substance use or enforcement change in Sunset Park this week.
evidence: 6 drinking complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (380% spike, z-score 3.96)
No corroborating Reddit or local news coverage yet—making this an emerging, under-reported issue
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD or community board about whether enforcement posture changed or if actual street drinking is increasing
Canvass local business owners, parks, and transit hubs to assess whether residents perceive a recent change in visible alcohol use

themes_detail.label: Dead Animals Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints hit 13 last week, up 1056% from an 8-week baseline of 1.1 per week (z-score: 8.18)—a major sanitation and public health signal that warrants immediate investigation into possible disease, predator activity, or disposal failures.
evidence: 13 dead animal complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1056% spike, z-score 8.18, severity: high)
Sustained elevated spike—indicates systemic issue, not random event
Overlaps with elevated 'Unsanitary Condition' complaints (277 over 90 days) and 'Dirty Condition' complaints (277 over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks, Department of Sanitation, and NYC Animal Care and Control to identify cause: disease outbreak, predators, or inadequate removal protocols
Report on public health implications and whether residents near parks or green spaces are reporting illnesses or pet concerns

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dogs Emergent Problem
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints exploded to 3 two weeks ago from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—raising questions about enforcement breakdown, park safety, or seasonal behavioral shift.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike, z-score 8.69, severity: high)
Converges with spike in 'Animal in a Park' complaints (5 last week vs. 1.0 baseline, 400% spike) and 'Noise - Park' complaints (4 three weeks ago vs. 0.4 baseline)
Multiple overlapping park-related complaints suggest a park safety or management issue
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Enforcement Patrol and dog owners about whether leash law enforcement has changed or if there's a new dog population in local parks
Investigate whether any parks lack adequate fencing or signage; connect with community board's standing request for park expansion/improvements

themes_detail.label: Park Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 3 weeks, park-related complaints have spiked across three categories: 'Noise - Park' (4 vs. 0.4 baseline, 967% spike), 'Animal in a Park' (5 last week vs. 1.0 baseline, 400% spike), and 'Unleashed Dog' (3 vs. 0.1 baseline, 2300% spike)—suggesting systemic park maintenance or management breakdown.
evidence: Noise - Park: 4 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 baseline (967% spike, z-score 5.21)
Animal in a Park: 5 complaints last week vs. 1.0 baseline (400% spike, z-score 4.62)
Unleashed Dog: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 baseline (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Community Board has submitted annual request for new or expanded parks/amenities to Parks and Recreation—suggesting pre-existing park capacity concerns
reporting_angles: Audit Parks Department staffing and maintenance schedules in Sunset Park's major parks; identify if staff cuts or vacancies coincide with complaint spike
Examine which specific parks are generating complaints; identify common factors (proximity to waterfront, residential density, enforcement presence)
Profile the four-year park expansion initiative (Brooklyn CD 7 Walk to Park Site Selection, currently in ULURP public review) and assess whether urgency has shifted due to current failures

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Failures
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints reached 9 three weeks ago, up 700% from a baseline of 1.1 per week (z-score: 4.47)—indicating either staffing shortfalls or a decline in sanitation service quality across the district.
evidence: 9 street sweeping complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score 4.47, severity: high)
Overlaps with elevated 'Dirty Condition' and 'Unsanitary Condition' complaints (277 each over 90 days), suggesting sustained sanitation underperformance
Spike timing (3 weeks ago) suggests issue may be moderating but warrants verification of current status
reporting_angles: Request Sanitation Department schedules and staffing data for Sunset Park routes; identify if crews were reassigned or reductions occurred
Interview residents and local business owners about whether streets feel cleaner now or if complaints have continued
